Handicapping utility · v4.75 · released 12 November 2026

Overlay Board

Upload a Brisnet data file (.DRF, .csv or .zip). Overlay Board lays out the whole card: past performances, scratches, money moves, and where the board likes a horse.

1 Bring in your data

Brisnet data file

Brisnet’s Single File export, or a multi-part card (the four-file .DRF/.DR2/.DR3/.DR4 set some tracks ship). A .zip is fine and is opened for you — for a multi-part card send the whole zip, since the four files only work as a set. If .drf looks greyed out in the picker, rename it to .csv; the parser reads the contents, not the name.

Apply scratches from the Equibase feed

Load the data file above first, then choose the track’s Changes & Scratches feed or paste it below. Scratches are ticked automatically by race and program number. Rider changes are flagged on the card, with the new rider’s meet record where the file has one.

2 Check & edit entries

ML odds comes in with the file. Final starts empty — fill it in at the track; it never overwrites the morning line. Surface fit and Class are optional. Tick Scr for a scratch and rebuild the card: scratched horses drop out and the field renormalizes.

▦ Race decision board

The decision for each race and nothing else. Tap a horse for its past performances; every warning, contender and table is under Race facts.

🖨 Printable page

The whole card on one page. Save as PDF makes a clean decision sheet (every race's pick, bet line and full field) and opens your phone's share sheet, where you can Save to Files, AirDrop, email or print it. Print uses your browser's own print sheet, which some phones don't show.

? How to read this

The tabs

Decisions — one card per race: the decision and nothing else. Race card — the full field, race by race, with Full field and True contenders only buttons. Race facts — one fold per race: the warnings and the reason for the pick, every horse side by side, contenders vs pretenders, form detail, and previous meetings. Tap any horse name for its full past performances. Printable page — the card laid out for printing, with a Save as PDF button that makes a clean decision sheet and opens your phone's share sheet.

Reading a decision card

Top row: race number, distance and surface, class, number of runners, and the board's chance for its pick — that horse's share of the field's chance, worked out from the rank score and case score and then adjusted for the warnings (not a win probability or a price). The pick is the board's final selection after the warnings are weighed.

Confidence level: the pick's blended chance — the morning-line price and the board's own chance weighed together, about 2 to 1. HIGH is 45% or more, MODERATE 35% to 45%, LOW under 35%; if AI(2) ranks a different horse first, the level is one step lower. A race with a win bet reads BET RACE. Confidence says how likely the pick is to win; it is not a price check, which is what the bet tiers do.

The plan: PLAY — WIN BET ONLY (the win bet stands, exotics stay off), PLAY, or SKIP, with the reason printed under it. Then the tier line and its tested win percentage (see Tiers and percentages), the value-price line on win bets, the AI(1)/AI(2) line (do the two other methods agree with the pick), a one-line pace note, a race-type chip (how often the board's picks win in that type of race), and warning chips. A chip opens that race's facts.

When the pick moves, and when to trust the morning line

In a race with no bet, if the second-best chance is within 10 points of the leader and that horse is the morning-line favourite or AI(2)'s top pick, and has not faded late in most of its last three races, the pick moves to it; the card says so. A pick that faded late in most of its last three races drops one confidence step. The chip "Morning line reliable here" or "not reliable here" says whether the favourite has been worth trusting in races of this kind (turf, allowance and stakes, short-priced favourites and fields with no first-time starters, against claiming races, first-time-starter favourites and long-priced favourites). On a bet, the card also notes a poor record on today's surface and a race graded RED. The one exception is a readiness check: there is no win bet on a horse whose last race finished 7th or worse and that has no win in its last 6 starts. In a low-confidence race, Race facts also adds a second look: the next four horses by chance after the pick, with a tag where one is the morning-line favourite, AI(2)'s top pick or the top earner per start. These notes change no other bet. In Race facts each horse also shows, in bold, the signals it carries: AI(2)'s pick, #1 on ability, #1 on chance, morning-line favourite, top earner per start, and #1 on rank score. A contender that ran within 45 days and worked within 14 days is also labelled FRESH, with the two dates. A horse carrying two or more is shown in solid. These tags change no chance, pick, tier or bet. Race facts also say whether the race shapes up as a two-horse race or is wide open, from how much of the chance the top two horses hold.

Where the board makes no win bet

There is no win bet in a maiden special weight race or in a wide-open race (the top two horses hold under 43% of the chance), whatever the tier, and none on a horse whose last race finished 7th or worse with no win in its last 6. Race facts says so on those races. The pick and its confidence are still shown.

Winner details only

The default view shows only what the history has shown to help pick winners. It hides the pace lines, the poor-record-on-today's-surface note, the CORE lines, the second-look list, and the signal tags for rank score and top earner. The FRESH label stays. A line in Race facts names the rank-score leader when it has two or more warning signs (a rank score of 5 or worse, a lead under 3 points, not the morning-line favourite) or is not the pick. The Winner details only button switches everything back on.

First-time starters

In a lightly raced field a first-time starter is ranked by its morning line, but never above the best horse that has raced: it sits just behind that horse.

A first-time starter has no past performances to read, so the board never names one as its pick. When one leads the ranking the card says so and gives no pick and no bet; the best horse that has raced is listed in Race facts. In the past performances the Run column shows a past race's running line — positions at the first call, second call, stretch and finish, with the field size — and the early-speed note quotes the last race's running line so the number can be checked against it.

Warning chips

Selection reversal — the board's pick differs from the plain ranking (figures, Prime Power and morning line). Reversals are the weaker races; a reversal alone does not justify a wager. Wide open and Two-horse — see When the two methods disagree. Fragile favourite — a short-priced favourite with signs it can finish out of the money. Debut runner to watch — a first-time starter the odds-maker rates as live. Close call — the best rival's blended chance is within 5 points of the pick's, so the race is close to a coin flip between the two. Lone speed / Contested pace — how the early speed sets up. Each chip's full text is in that race's Race facts fold.

Rank score and case score

RS (rank score) adds the horse's rank on the figures, Prime Power and morning line; lower is better. Penalties are then added: ⊖ fade signals add 5 each, ⬇ trouble or surface flags add 10, and "not competitive at level" adds 3. CS (case score) ranks horses by their favourable minus unfavourable race facts — the For and Against lists; the case tally is that difference.

Saving a PDF

On the Printable page tab, Save as PDF writes a decision sheet — every race's pick, chance, confidence, bet line, warnings and a full-field table — and opens the share sheet so you can Save to Files, AirDrop, email or print it. If your browser has no share sheet, the PDF downloads or opens in a new tab.

The figure favourite frozen rule

Only the morning-line favourite is ever eligible — nobody else can be named. It becomes the figure favourite under one condition: it also holds the field's sole highest mean of its last three speed figures. A tie at the top doesn't count. Second on that figure doesn't count. Needs three runners in the race carrying a figure at all.

That's the whole rule. Nothing about readability, pace, works, or barn entries touches it — those all sit next to the figure favourite as information, never as a gate.

Price play fallback rule

Used only when no figure favourite fires: the morning-line favourite is second in the field on career earnings per start. A separate, weaker line — logged, never treated the same as a figure favourite.

Contenders / Questionable / Pretenders

Every runner sorted into one of three buckets based on price and form evidence. Contenders are live. Questionable horses lack clean evidence either way. Pretenders are priced out with nothing to rescue them. This is what "Also with a shot" and Top 4 both draw from.

Top 4 probable

The four highest-ranked Contenders by figure, shown per race under Race facts ("Top 4 probable, with form detail"). Tap any name to open its full past performances; tap the name again inside that view to come straight back.

Also with a shot

The rest of the field, ordered by the same read that flagged Army's Marauder — competitive-at-today's-level ratio first, earnings per start as the tiebreaker. Not by price. A horse with no comparable starts to judge sorts to the end, not the top.

Worth a second look — pace display only

Fires when the figure favourite's own last three starts show a fading majority (2 of 3, read from the pace figures below) and a genuine Contender in the same field shows the opposite. Doesn't change the figure favourite.

When the two methods disagree

The POTENTIAL line says what the agreement of AI(1) and AI(2) has meant. When they pick the same horse: STRONG (the pick's chance is 35% or more and AI(2)'s share 65% or more), GOOD (chance 35% or more, a lower share) or LIMITED (chance under 35%). When they pick different horses it is SPLIT, and the line gives the field size, because in a split another horse wins more often as the field grows. Whether the race is a two-horse race or wide open is a separate fact, from how much of the chance the top two horses hold (Shape of the race).

Tiers and percentages

Each race shows a tier for its named horse and the share of such horses that won on the cards in the pack: Tier 1 DEFINITIVE with a clear #1 in a race that passes the race screen (79%) · Tier 2 DEFINITIVE (72%) · Tier 3 SOLID PICK (53%) · Tier 4 CONDITIONAL, when 2-1 or higher at post (82%) · Tier 5 top pick with HIGH confidence, no win bet (72%) · Tier 6 top pick with MODERATE confidence, no win bet (50%) · Tier 7 top pick with LOW confidence, no win bet (27%). Confidence is the pick's blended chance, the morning-line price and the board's own chance weighed together: HIGH is 45% or more (such picks won 80% of the time), MODERATE 35% to 45% (52%), LOW under 35% (29%). When AI(2) ranks a different horse first the level drops one step. Tiers 1-3 are bets, Tier 4 only at 2-1 or higher; Tiers 5-7 carry no win-bet edge and say so. These are past results on the pack's cards, which the rules were built from; on new cards expect them to run a few points lower. When you record winners on the race cards, the percentages blend in your own results, and the scorecard at the top of the board shows how each tier, bet type and confidence level is doing.

BET — SOLID PICK

A win bet on the top-ranked horse when neither DEFINITIVE nor CONDITIONAL applies, and either (A) its morning line is 8-5 or shorter, it has the best Prime Power in the field, at most one no-finish trip comment in its last four, and the race is not low priority; or (B) its morning line is 2-1 or shorter, the field has 8 or fewer runners, it has the best last figure in the field, and its case tally is +4 or better.

Figure leader and value dropper

Further win bets, independent of the tiers. ALLOWANCE PICK: the top pick in an allowance race, at 2-1 or higher, when the race has no other bet. FIGURE LEADER: a horse with the best 3-race figure average and a case of +6 or better in a field of 8 or fewer. VALUE DROPPER was retired in v4.29: once the fair-odds comparison was corrected, it no longer paid. Both stand even in races otherwise marked SKIP; exactas in those races stay off.

Value price (stake guide)

Every Tier 1–4 win bet shows a value price worked out from the board's own chance for the horse. At that price or longer the board suggests a double stake; below it a single stake. On past cards this kept every bet and returned more than flat staking, because the well-priced bets have paid best. The board never names dollar amounts.

Downgraded bets

A SOLID PICK or CONDITIONAL horse with two or more Against items drops one tier: a SOLID PICK becomes a win bet only at 2-1 or higher, and a CONDITIONAL becomes no win bet. A CONDITIONAL bet also needs a morning line of 2-1 or longer: it never relies on a horse drifting up to 2-1. The tier line says it was downgraded and why. DEFINITIVE bets (Tiers 1-2) are not downgraded; a vulnerable one is flagged instead.

Strong challengers

The tier line names any strong challenger: a contender that beats the top-ranked horse on two or more of Prime Power, last figure and early speed. Their edges are in Race Facts under EDGES OVER #1.

Ability and fair odds

FAIR (DATA) is the price each horse's own record would justify, worked out from the past performances alone, with no odds of any kind: its 3-race, last and best figures against the best in today's field, its Prime Power against the best, its early-speed points, how often it was in the money in its last four starts, whether it won last time, any ⬇ flags or ⊖ fades, and whether it is a first-time starter. ABILITY is the horse's rank in the field on those same fair odds — #1 has the strongest record. Under FAIR, ML shorter means the morning line rates the horse better than its record does; ML longer means the record rates it better than the morning line.

Concurrence — AI(1) / AI(2)

AI(1) is the top horse in this board's ranking. AI(2) is the top horse in a second, independent ranking ported into this file and run on the same field and scratches; it weighs recent figures, form, pace, surface and class and does not use the morning line. CONCURRENT: both put the same horse first. DIFFERENT: they disagree. A figure favourite that AI(2) does not rank first is not bet. Agreement is shown as information; it is not a bet on its own.

Readability display only

How thick the field's data actually is — green, yellow (thin), or red (blind). Never suppresses or overrides the figure favourite. A blind-record figure favourite still fires; the color just tells you how much you're trusting a thin field when it does.

"Too close to call" display only

Flags when the top few horses are within 3 points of each other on Prime Power — a different rating from the speed figure the figure favourite uses, so this can fire even when the figure favourite's own figure has a clean, sole leader. It describes the field; it doesn't change the figure favourite.

Reading a past-performance line

Date, track, distance, surface, post, class move (▲ tougher · = about the same · ▼ easier than today), finish, who won/placed/showed, the BRIS speed figure, Pace, class text, trip comment.

Pace shows the BRIS pace-call figures for that race in order (2-call, 4-call, 6-call, 8-call, late pace — same rating scale as Speed) plus a plain read of the shape from the running line: closed late if the horse gained 2 or more lengths between the second call and the finish, faded late if it lost 2 or more, even shape otherwise. A fact about that one race, not a score. See "Worth a second look" above for where the shape is used.

Race card columns

Form arrow — beaten-lengths trend across the last few starts, oldest to newest: green ▲ closing (finishing closer than before), red ▼ widening (falling further behind), dash flat. Tap the arrow to reveal the actual sequence. A display fact, same as pace.

Speed column with LONE tag — Quirin speed points, BRIS's own 0–8 scale for early-speed tendency, not a speed figure. LONE means the top horse is at least 5 on that scale and at least 2 points clear of the next — likely gets an uncontested early lead. The 8-point scale has nothing to do with field size.

The numeric speed column (e.g. "94 (88)") — the actual BRIS speed figure: last race, best figure in parentheses if different. This is the number the figure favourite rule is built on.

Tapping around

Any horse name with a dotted underline opens its full past performances. Inside that view, tap the horse's own name again to return to wherever you came from — a decision card, the Race card or Race facts. Closing normally (the ✕ or tapping outside) does the same.
